abuse_act_body: We can suspend a project: our relays stop routing its address, and it can no longer register or report in. We cannot delete anything from the owner's server. For a project on a custom domain, also tell the domain's owner or registrar.
abuse_contact_unavailable: The address could not be loaded. Try again later.
abuse_intro: Promptbook projects run on their owners' own servers. Each one is reachable at an address under our project domain or at a custom domain. If one of them hosts phishing, malware or anything else that harms people, tell us.
abuse_report_item_address: the full address (URL) of the page, including the project's hostname;
abuse_report_item_evidence: a screenshot, or the message that led you there, if you have one.
abuse_report_item_what: what the page does or asks for, and when you saw it;
abuse_report_response: We confirm every report and act on a confirmed one within hours. Do not send us passwords or other secrets you may have typed into the page.
abuse_security: Security vulnerabilities in Promptbook itself go to the same address. Machine-readable details are in
abuse_see_can: We can see which account a project belongs to, whether it is online, how much traffic passes through our relays, and the page it shows to anyone who opens it without signing in. We check that public page ourselves, as any visitor would.
abuse_see_cannot: We cannot see what a project shows to signed-in users or what its traffic contains: the connection is encrypted end to end between the visitor's browser and the owner's server, and our relays only pass it on.
abuse_see_title: What we can and cannot see

Hi,

Good news: you can now use {engine}. Someone on the project approved you.

Open it here and sign in with the passkey you created for it:

{link}

Tip: bookmark it. The project has its own address, {hostname}, and you can always open it from the dashboard too.

Hi,

A colleague is waiting for access to {engine}: {requester}.

To let them in:

1. Open the project's Members page:
   {link}
2. Ask {requester} for the 6-digit code on their screen.
3. Find their request, type in the code and approve it.

Only someone already on the project can approve. If you don't recognise this request, decline it there.

Hi,

Someone, probably you, wanted to sign in to Promptbook with this address. You already have an account.

Sign in with your passkey. If it is on another device, such as your phone, your browser can use it from there:

{signInLink}

Lost your device? Recover access by email:

{recoveryLink}

If this wasn't you, ignore this email. Nothing changes without your passkey.

email_invite_passkey_body:
Hi,

Open this link on the device you want to use, add a passkey, and you can join {org}. The link works once and expires in 15 minutes:

{link}

For your safety, this signs out your other devices, and for 72 hours nobody can remove projects or change billing ownership on this account.

If you did not ask for this, you can ignore this email. Nothing changes.

{link}

trust_promise: Your agents, chats and files stay on your own server. We connect you to them, but we can't read them.
trust_path_browser_body: Seals everything it sends so that only your project can open it.
trust_path_relay_body: Passes the sealed traffic on to your project. It can't open it.
trust_path_engine_body: Holds your data and its keys. The connection opens only here.
trust_path_dashboard_body: Off to the side: your account, billing, who you invited, and your projects' addresses and status. Never what is inside them.
trust_cannot_see_body: Your agents, chats and files live on your project. We never store them, not even encrypted.
trust_cannot_open_body: It is encrypted all the way from your browser to your project. Our relays only pass it on and hold none of its keys.
trust_cannot_change_body: The app you use is signed, publicly logged and the same for everyone. Your project checks it before serving it and installs only updates that are already public.
trust_cannot_admit_body: Everyone signs in with a passkey made for your project. Only your project can add people or make someone its owner; your Promptbook account grants nothing inside it.
trust_cannot_card_body: You pay on Stripe's own pages, so your card details go straight to Stripe and never reach Promptbook.
trust_can_status_title: See that your project is well
trust_can_status_body: Every minute your project sends us a few numbers: whether it is online, its version, how busy it is, how many agents and members it has, and whether setup or an update is waiting. Never names or text.
trust_can_stop_body: We can cut the connection, and remove people who joined through this dashboard unless your project's owner turns that off. Even then, or if we are ever down, your agents keep running and nothing is lost; you just can't reach the project through us until we're back.
trust_check_security: Your project's Security page shows which app it runs, the app's public log entry, and exactly what your project last sent us.
trust_check_fingerprint: Each project has a fingerprint, a small pattern and code that looks the same here and on the project. If they differ, enter nothing there and open your project from this dashboard.
trust_check_source: The software your project runs is open source:
